drafts.spl: index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 ParentImage="*WINWORD.EXE" Image="*\\powershell.exe" | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)\\s-e(nc|ncodedcommand)?\\s") OR match(CommandLine, "(?i)-enc") | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)-enc") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine values(ParentImage) as ParentImage values(Image) as Image values(User) as User by Computer

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1
| where match(ParentImage, "(?i)[\\\\/]winword[.]exe$")
| where (match(Image, "(?i)[\\\\/]powershell[.]exe$") OR match(OriginalFileName, "(?i)^powershell[.]exe$"))
| where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(^|\\s)-e(c|n|nc|nco|ncod|ncode|ncoded|ncodedc|ncodedco|ncodedcom|ncodedcomm|ncodedcomma|ncodedcomman|ncodedcommand)?(\\s|:)\\s*[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}")
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine values(ParentImage) as ParentImage values(Image) as Image values(OriginalFileName) as OriginalFileName values(User) as User by Computer

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 WINWORD powershell
| where match(ParentImage, "(?i)[\\\\/]winword[.]exe$")
| where (match(Image, "(?i)[\\\\/]powershell[.]exe$") OR match(OriginalFileName, "(?i)^powershell[.]exe$"))
| where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(^|\\s)[-/]e(c|n|nc|nco|ncod|ncode|ncoded|ncodedc|ncodedco|ncodedcom|ncodedcomm|ncodedcomma|ncodedcomman|ncodedcommand)?[\\s:]+[\"']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}")
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine values(Image) as Image values(OriginalFileName) as OriginalFileName values(ParentImage) as ParentImage by Computer User ProcessGuid

gates.gate_spl: search index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 | where match(ParentImage, "(?i)[\\\\/]winword[.]exe$") | where (match(Image, "(?i)[\\\\/]powershell[.]exe$") OR match(OriginalFileName, "(?i)^powershell[.]exe$")) | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(^|\\s)[-/]e(c|n|nc|nco|ncod|ncode|ncoded|ncodedc|ncodedco|ncodedcom|ncodedcomm|ncodedcomma|ncodedcomman|ncodedcommand)?[\\s:]+[\"']*[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | bin _time span=20m | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine values(Image) as Image values(OriginalFileName) as OriginalFileName values(ParentImage) as ParentImage by _time Computer User | sort 0 - count

findings.detail: The effective encoding filter is the second clause `| where match(CommandLine, "(?i)-enc")`, which requires the literal substring "enc" to appear after the dash. The first `where ... OR ...` line is dead (the AND with the second where negates its broader `-e`/`\s-e\s` branch). PowerShell accepts unambiguous abbreviations of -EncodedCommand such as `-e`, `-ec`, and `-en` (and `-enco`), all of which are heavily used by Office-macro droppers. `-ec SQBF...` and `-e SQBF...` do NOT contain "enc" and are completely missed, even though they are the exact attack step (WINWORD->powershell -EncodedCommand base64).
findings.fix_hint: Match on the switch prefix, e.g. match the regex `(?i)(^|\s)-e(c|n|nc|nco|ncod|ncode|ncoded|ncodedc|ncodedco|ncodedcom|ncodedcomm|ncodedcomma|ncodedcomman|ncodedcommand)?(\s|:)` requiring a base64-looking argument, and drop the contradictory double where.

findings.detail: Child process is filtered only on `Image="*\\powershell.exe"`. A macro can drop/copy powershell.exe under another name (e.g. C:\Users\Public\msupdate.exe) and launch it; the Image path no longer ends in powershell.exe so the whole search fails, even though OriginalFileName still reports PowerShell.EXE. OriginalFileName is ingested (sample shows `PowerShell.EXE`) but unused.
findings.fix_hint: Add `OR OriginalFileName="powershell.exe"` (or `OR OriginalFileName="pwsh.dll"/"powershell.exe"`) to the child-process condition so renamed interpreters are still caught.

findings.detail: Redundant/contradictory logic: `| where match(...\s-e(nc|ncodedcommand)?\s) OR match(...-enc) | where match(...-enc)`. The second where ANDs `-enc`, so the OR in the first line can never contribute — its intent to catch `-e <blob>` is nullified. Also `(?i)-enc` is an unanchored substring that can match inside a file path or the base64 blob (base64 alphabet includes e,n,c), risking stray matches.
findings.fix_hint: Collapse to a single anchored where on the switch boundary and require a base64 argument; remove the useless first clause.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -ec SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAIABOAGUAdAAuAFcAZQBiAEMAbABpAGUAbgB0ACkA</Data><Data Name='OriginalFileName'>PowerShell.EXE</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Identical attack step (WINWORD->powershell, base64 blob) but using the valid `-ec` abbreviation of -EncodedCommand instead of `-enc`/-EncodedCommand. The `(?i)-enc` where clause finds no 'enc' substring, so the search misses it entirely. Must match.

Macro copies powershell.exe to C:\Users\Public\msupdate.exe and launches it with -enc. Image no longer ends in powershell.exe so the Image filter fails, but OriginalFileName is still PowerShell.EXE. Same attack step; must match via OriginalFileName.

findings.detail: The CommandLine regex ends in `(\s|:)\s*[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}`, so after the parameter it demands that a base64 character come next (optionally preceded by whitespace). PowerShell fully accepts the encoded blob in quotes: `-enc "SQBF..."` or `-enc 'SQBF...'` (the quotes are stripped at parse time). With a quote as the next char the regex never reaches the base64 class and the event is completely missed, even though this is the exact attack step (WINWORD->powershell -EncodedCommand base64). A macro that concatenates a quoted argument string trivially produces this.
findings.fix_hint: After the separator allow an optional opening quote before the base64 class, e.g. `(\s|:)\s*["']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}`.

findings.detail: The base generating search is only `index=wineventlog sourcetype=... EventCode=1` with all narrowing done in four `where match()` regex clauses. EventCode=1 (process creation) is one of the highest-volume Sysmon channels; in production every process-create event in the window is retrieved and regex-scanned. None of the literal anchors (`winword`, `powershell`, `enc`/`encoded`) are pushed into the base search so Splunk cannot prune at index time.
findings.fix_hint: Add index-time terms to the base search, e.g. `(WINWORD OR winword) (powershell OR PowerShell) (enc OR Encoded)` before the where clauses to cut the scanned event set.

findings.detail: Final `stats ... by Computer` groups solely on Computer and collapses CommandLine/ParentImage/Image/User into multivalue sets. Two distinct user sessions or repeated executions on one host merge into a single alert row, and min/max times span unrelated events, reducing triage fidelity. This does not cause a miss of the attack step.
findings.fix_hint: Group by Computer, User, ProcessGuid (or add ProcessGuid/UtcTime to the by-clause) to keep executions distinct.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -enc "SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAIABOAGUAdAAuAFcAZQBiAEMAbABpAGUAbgB0ACkA"</Data><Data Name='OriginalFileName'>PowerShell.EXE</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Identical WINWORD->powershell -enc base64 attack, but the base64 blob is wrapped in double quotes (valid PowerShell). The CommandLine regex expects a base64 char immediately after the separator and sees `"` instead, so the event is not matched. The search must still fire.

findings.detail: Base generating search is still only `index=wineventlog sourcetype=... EventCode=1` with all narrowing in four `where match()` regex clauses. EventCode=1 (process create) is the highest-volume Sysmon channel; every process-create event in the window is retrieved and regex-scanned. No literal anchor (winword, powershell, enc/encoded, EncodedCommand) is pushed into the base search, so Splunk cannot prune at index time. Persists from prior findings; unchanged by the regex fix.
findings.fix_hint: Add index-time constraints to the base search, e.g. `(ParentImage="*winword.exe" OR ParentCommandLine="*WINWORD.EXE*") (Image="*powershell.exe" OR OriginalFileName=powershell.exe) CommandLine="*e*"` before the where-regex refinement so TSIDX pruning applies.

findings.detail: Final `stats ... by Computer User` collapses CommandLine/ParentImage/Image/OriginalFileName into multivalue sets and uses min/max time across all events for that pair. Repeated executions or distinct Office->powershell chains on one host/user merge into a single row with a time span covering unrelated events, lowering triage fidelity. Does not cause a miss of the attack step.
findings.fix_hint: Group by additional fields (ProcessGuid or bin(_time) buckets, CommandLine) or emit per-event to preserve each chain for triage.

findings.detail: Renamed-binary coverage for powershell.exe relies solely on `match(OriginalFileName, "(?i)^powershell[.]exe$")` when Image is renamed. If the Sysmon config does not populate OriginalFileName (field absence) or the PE VERSIONINFO OriginalFilename is modified, a renamed powershell.exe launched by WINWORD with an encoded command is missed. The PE-metadata tamper is advanced and renaming alone preserves OriginalFileName, so impact is limited.
findings.fix_hint: Also key on Hashes/ImageLoaded of System.Management.Automation, or require OriginalFileName=powershell.exe be present and alert on Image/OriginalFileName mismatch as a secondary signal.
